title: Chapter 5: Culture, Art & Literature of J&K

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Rishi Order of Kashmiri Sufism was established by Sheikh Noor-ud-Din Wali (Nund Reshi), blending Sufi principles with local traditions.
Kashmiri music is highlighted by Sufiyana Kalam and Chakri, whereas Jammu is noted for Dogri folk music and Kud dance.
Traditional Kashmiri cuisine features Wazwan, a multi-course feast meticulously prepared by a master chef called a Vasta Waza.
Kalhana's Rajatarangini stands as one of the most prominent Sanskrit historical chronicles detailing the rulers of Kashmir.
Ladakhi culture incorporates distinctive Buddhist traditions, including monastery festivals featuring sacred Chham dances.

cells: Mother tongue of Kashmiri Muslims & Pandits; Sharada script (ancient), now mostly in Nastaliq (Urdu script) & Devanagari; 8th Schedule language
Language of Jammu region; also 8th Schedule; Dogra community; Takri script (traditional); Devanagari used now
Spoken in hilly Jammu; similar to Himachali; not in 8th Schedule yet

items: J&K officially added 5 official languages in September 2020: Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, English
Kashmiriyat: Syncretic culture of Kashmir — blend of Hindu and Muslim traditions; tolerance, shared shrines
Lal Ded (Lalleshwari / Lal Arifa): 14th century mystic poet; wrote Vakhs (mystic verses); Shaiva devotee; first prominent Kashmiri literary figure; revered by both Hindus and Muslims
Sheikh Noor-ud-Din Wali (Nand Rishi): 14th-15th century; founder of Rishi order in Kashmir; patron saint; shrine at Charar-e-Sharief
Rishi Order: Indigenous Sufi tradition of Kashmir; emphasized nature, vegetarianism, simple life
Shah Hamadan (Mir Syed Ali Hamdani): 14th century; introduced Islam widely; brought craftsmen from Persia; Khanqah-e-Moula in Srinagar
Habba Khatoon: 16th century Kashmiri poetess; 'Nightingale of Kashmir'; wife of Yusuf Shah Chak
Sufiana Kalam: Classical Kashmiri music; Persian-influenced; semi-classical; accompanied by Santoor
Chakri: Folk music of Jammu region; group performance; percussion heavy
Ladishah: Satirical folk songs; social commentary; performed by wandering minstrels
Wanwun: Traditional marriage songs sung by women in Kashmir
Rauf: Traditional dance-song performed by women in Kashmir during Eid; semi-circular formation
Dumhal: Wattal community tribal dance; Jammu & Kashmir; masks; performed at Dargah of Hazrat Sheikh Ahmad
Bhand Pather: Traditional theatre of Kashmir; blend of dance, music, satire; Bhand (clown) is central character
Hikat: Folk song of Kashmir; boatmen's songs

blocks.content: Chapter 5: Culture, Art & Literature of J&K

items: Dogri Folk Songs: Heer-Ranjha, Mirza-Sahiban in local style
Dogri Pahari Dance: Performed during local festivals
Kud Dance: Performed in honor of Gods; Jammu hills; torch-lit night dance
Shondol: Royal ceremonial dance of Ladakh — nominated for UNESCO; women wear elaborate headgear
Jabro: Traditional Ladakhi folk dance
Cham Dance: Masked dance at Buddhist monasteries (Hemis, Lamayuru)

cells: Leh; June-July; at Hemis Monastery; Cham masked dance; birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava; biggest festival of Ladakh
Srinagar; April; Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden; Asia's largest tulip garden; 1.5 million tulips
Kashmir Pandits celebrate with great fervor; main Kashmiri Pandit festival
Kashmiri New Year; first day of Navratri in chaitra; Kashmiri Pandits
Ganderbal; Jyeshtha month; Kashmiri Pandits gather at temple spring
Shravan month (July-Aug); lakhs of pilgrims; ice Shiva Linga
September; Leh; archery, polo, mask dances, traditional sports
Jammu; at Bahu Fort; Navratras; largest fair in Jammu

items: Wazwan: Elaborate multi-course feast; 36 dishes; centerpiece of Kashmiri Muslim wedding cuisine; Waza (chef) prepares it; lamb is primary meat
Rogan Josh: Slow-cooked lamb with Kashmiri spices; GI tag; red color from Kashmiri chili
Gushtaba: Large meatballs in creamy yogurt gravy; king of Wazwan
Tabak Maaz: Fried ribs; crispy lamb dish
Dum Aloo: Baby potatoes in spicy gravy; very popular
Haak Saag: Kashmiri collard greens cooked in mustard oil
Kahwa: Traditional Kashmiri green tea with saffron, cardamom, cinnamon, almonds — served in Samovar
Sheer Chai (Nun Chai): Pink salty tea; unique to Kashmir; with milk and sodium bicarbonate
Modur Pulao: Sweet saffron rice with dry fruits
Rajma Chawal: Red kidney beans with rice; iconic Jammu dish
Ambal: Sweet & sour pumpkin dish
Khatta Meat: Sour mutton curry
Mitha Chawal: Sweet saffron rice for festivals
Kalhana composed Rajatarangini in Sanskrit during the reign of King Jayasimha.
Rouf and Bhand Pather are major traditional folk arts from the Kashmir Valley frequently asked in JKSSB exams.
Kud dance is a ritualistic folk dance performed in the Jammu region to honor local deities (Lok Devtas).
Sheikh Noor-ud-Din Wali is popularly revered as Nund Reshi and Alamdar-e-Kashmir.
Thukpa: Noodle soup; Tibetan-influenced; popular in Ladakh & across J&K
Tsampa: Roasted barley flour; staple of Ladakh
Butter Tea (Po Cha): Salt butter tea; traditional Ladakhi beverage
Skyu: Thick pasta soup with root vegetables
Chang: Local barley beer

cells: 12th century; wrote Rajatarangini (Chronicle of Kings); first Indian historian
14th century; Kashmiri Shaiva mystic poetess; 'Vakhs' in Kashmiri
20th century Kashmiri poet; Nund Rishi influence
First modern Dogri poet; Padma Shri awardee

items: Khanqah-e-Moula: Srinagar; largest wooden structure in Kashmir; built by Shah Hamadan; on Jhelum bank
Hazratbal Shrine: Dal Lake, Srinagar; contains holy relic (hair) of Prophet Muhammad
Jama Masjid Srinagar: Largest mosque; Indo-Saracenic style; 700-year-old; Makhdum Sahib area
Shankaracharya Temple: Srinagar hill; ancient Shiva temple; 'Jyesthesvara'
Martand Sun Temple: Mattan, Anantnag; 8th century; largest temple complex in Kashmir
Avantipora Ruins: Awantipora, Pulwama; 9th century; two temples built by Avantivarman
Raghunath Temple: Jammu; largest temple complex in North India; dedicated to Lord Rama; built by Maharaja Gulab Singh & Ranbir Singh
Ranbireshwar Temple: Jammu; large Shiva temple with 12 Jyotirlingas replicas
Bahu Fort: Jammu; oldest fort; Kali temple inside; Tawi river bank
Mubarak Mandi Palace Complex: Jammu; historical royal palace complex of Dogra rulers
Hemis Monastery: Leh; 17th century; Drukpa Kagyu sect; largest & richest in Ladakh; Hemis Tsedup
Thikse Monastery: 12 km from Leh; resembles Lhasa Potala; Gelugpa sect
Lamayuru Monastery: Oldest in Ladakh; 'Moonland' landscape
Alchi Monastery: Indus Valley; 10th century; unique wall paintings; oldest in Ladakh
Leh Palace: 17th century; 9-storey; built by King Sengge Namgyal; overlooks Leh town
Basohli: Town in Kathua; famous for Basohli paintings; Ragamala, Ramayana, Bhagavata Purana themes
